turns.title: Callbacks return to the session that spawned the run
turns.hypothesis: A product loop can explain Terrarium's current callback contract without pretending the content is containment evidence.
turns.attempt: Create one public-safe product campaign turn with an editorial SVG illustration and explicit non-evidence framing.
turns.result: The app now has an active campaign item about run-ID-bound callback delivery. It is labeled as product content, not proof of a containment run.
turns.adaptation: Add the next active campaign turn for another durable execution primitive.
turns.story: One bounded child run should return its terminal event to the session that asked for it, not every session in the same channel.

turns.title: Exit 0 is not task success
turns.hypothesis: A public campaign turn can make Terrarium's most important success rule clear without exposing child output or private prompts.
turns.attempt: Add one active campaign turn showing that a clean process exit and a verified task receipt are separate facts.
turns.result: The active campaign now explains why Terrarium can mark a child inconclusive even when the child process exits 0: no correlated receipt means no accepted task success.
turns.adaptation: Add a turn for explicit batch fan-out or cancellation next.
turns.story: A process can exit cleanly while the task failed to prove completion. Terrarium keeps those facts separate.

turns.title: A batch is not a swarm
turns.hypothesis: The active campaign should explain that Terrarium batch work is flat, explicit, and still made of ordinary independent runs.
turns.attempt: Add one campaign turn and illustration showing a parent launching several separate runs and joining terminal states with all, any, quorum, or race.
turns.result: The campaign now distinguishes batch fan-out from hidden role agents, chains, or swarms. Every child remains one bounded run with its own receipt.
turns.adaptation: Add the next turn for cancellation or doctor/attention signals.
turns.story: One explicit batch call can start several independent runs, but Terrarium does not invent a hidden workflow graph behind the parent.
